 This article first appeared on GuruFocus . 
 Release Date: November 02, 2026 
 For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript . 
 Positive Points 
 Paramount acquisition integration is fully complete, with all claims running on the Matrix platform and group customers migrated, enabling like-to-like comparisons. 
 Consolidated H1 revenue grew 13.8% to INR492 crores, EBITDA rose 19% to INR97.2 crores, and reported PAT surged 60% to INR49.2 crores. 
 EBITDA margin recovered to 20.4% in Q2 FY27, up 331 bps YoY, driven by integration synergies, lower people costs, and AI tool deployment. 
 Technology platform and HPA business revenue grew nearly 70% YoY in H1, processing over 7 million claims, with significant incremental revenue potential from value-added bundles. 
 Debt-free balance sheet with strong cash flows, and a capital allocation policy to return ~50% of cumulative adjusted free cash flow to shareholders over rolling five-year periods, starting with a INR49.3 crore buyback. 
 Negative Points 
 Retention rates have declined from historical 93-94% to ~90.5% due to churn in the Paramount book and a cyber incident, with recovery expected only over the next three to four quarters. 
 Same-store growth has slowed to 7-9% from historical 13-14%, impacted by weaker headcount growth in the IT/ITES sector and timing lags in other industries. 
 Q2 revenue growth was muted at 4.5% YoY (total income) and 3.9% (operating revenue), with India TPA revenue growing only 1.2% YoY, reflecting revenue recognition timing issues. 
 International business revenue growth was modest at 1.1% YoY in H1, despite expansion efforts and new memberships. 
 Group business, the largest revenue contributor, faces pressure from complex benefits, medical inflation, and fraud, with market share at 34.1% but growth dependent on employer headcount and benefit expansion. 
 Q & A Highlights

 Q : Given the investments in technology, cashless processing, and fraud detection, why doesn't the group retention rate exceed 93%94%? A : CEO Satish Gidugu explained that retention is reported on a stringent basis without adjustmentssmall companies that shut down, move employees to ESIC, or merge are counted as churn, which alone could add 100100 bps. A second factor is deliberate churn of accounts that are not commercially viable, and a third is a small percentage of clients whose expectations don't align. He noted that 93%94% is already high versus the industry, where acquired TPAs had retention of only 80%83%, and the company aims to exceed historical levels over time. 
 Story Continues Q : Why did India TPA revenue growth slow to low single digits in Q2, and how does premium growth translate into revenue growth? A : CEO Satish Gidugu said revenues are recognized on a 1/365 basis, so installment premiums and lost accounts continue to affect reported numbers with a lag. The company replaced about 80% of retention losses through new business, but revenue recognition timing means the impact will catch up over the next three to four quarters. He added that premium growth continues to outpace the market, and accounting revenue translation typically lags by two to three quarters. 
 Q : What is driving the decline in retention rates, and who has the business been lost to? A : CEO Satish Gidugu attributed the drop to churn in the large corporate book acquired from Paramount and the cyber incident in Paramount's systems last December, which affected renewals from January through April in the erstwhile Paramount book. He noted that some accounts are beginning to return and expressed confidence that retention will recover to historical levels on the new consolidated base within a few quarters. 
 Q : What are the growth expectations for revenues in H2 and FY28? A : CEO Satish Gidugu declined to provide specific guidance but reiterated that the TPA business will grow at or faster than the market from a premium share perspective, with timing affecting revenue accrual. He highlighted that monthly revenues have risen nearly 50% from Q1 FY26 to Q2 FY27, and contract liability (unearned revenue) increased by Rs 4050 crores from March to September, reflecting contracts already won and being serviced whose revenue is not yet in the P&L. 
 Q : How will retention return to 93%94%, and were PSU allocations lost? A : CEO Satish Gidugu said the Paramount integration is fully complete100% of corporates are served by Medi Assist systems and all claims run on the Matrix platform, with headcount about 800 people lower than at acquisition. He emphasized continuous innovation to improve the right to win in group business, noting the group business depends on employer choice rather than insurer reallocation. He did not specifically confirm PSU share losses but pointed to the integration and service improvements as the path back to historical retention. 
 Q : With margins at 20.4% post-Paramount integration, are there further levers, or is this the expected level? A : CEO Satish Gidugu said the Q2 EBITDA margin of 20.4% absorbs investments in the tech and international businesses, including overlapping costs and onboarding of new insurers whose revenues are yet to kick in. He maintained that steady-state margins in the core business are 20%23% and that returning there remains a key focus area. 
 Q : How could the Expense of Management (EOM) regulations affect Medi Assistare there pricing pressures or opportunities? A : CEO Satish Gidugu said the retail industry has already been through similar changes, with yields declining and the regulator holding insurers accountable for service delivery. He views EOM as a potential opportunity: insurers may look to outsource inefficient in-house claims servicing, and Medi Assist's blended 2.7% fee on group and retail is exceptional value. He added that the bigger insurer challenge is claims control while balancing customer experience, an area where Medi Assist's AI investments position it well. 
 Q : What is the scope of the technology platform opportunity, and how large are the seven onboarded insurers in terms of claims? A : CEO Satish Gidugu said the platform now offers solutions independent of the TPA offering, addressing insurer needs such as intelligent adjudication, policy complexity, audit trails, fraud control, and member experience. Most current platform revenue is pure SaaS claim processing (roughly Rs 100120 per claim), while value-added bundlesintelligent claims certification, network-as-a-service, and fraud waste abuseare contracted but not yet fully in revenues. These bundles could generate five to ten times the current revenue per claim, and the company has also decoupled bundles so insurers can use them on their own core systems. 
 Q : Why did group premiums managed grow only about 12% in Q2 versus 15% industry growth, and what is the outlook? A : CEO Satish Gidugu attributed the gap to higher churn from migrating tail-end Paramount accounts, the Paramount cyber incident affecting April renewals, and the 1/365 revenue recognition basis, which keeps lost customers' revenues in reported numbers for up to 365 days. The company replaced 75%80% of lost premiums through new corporate additions, and he expects reported retention and revenue growth to normalize over the next three to four quarters. 
 Q : How should investors think about the retail businessis it primarily a platform play, and how does monetization work? A : CEO Satish Gidugu said the platform gives Medi Assist an answer for insurers who want to own the customer experience, with the Matrix system of records as the base (about Rs 100120 per claim). Additional bundlesfraud detection, auto-adjudication, cashless and network management, member experienceare at different activation and contracting stages and should drive incremental revenue per existing customer. He also noted one insurer is using Medi Assist's intelligence bundle on its own core system, and EOM-driven cost optimization could deepen insurer engagement.
